character: Off-piste capital of the Alps. Real mountain town at the foot of Mont Blanc. 5 separate ski areas, legendary Vallee Blanche, mountaineering history since 1821.
description: Chamonix is a real year-round alpine town (population 10,000), not a purpose-built resort. It sits in the shadow of Mont Blanc (4,808m) — the highest peak in Western Europe. Skiing is split across 5 separate sectors (Brevent/Flegere, Grands Montets, Le Tour/Balme, Les Houches, and the Vallee Blanche glacier descent from Aiguille du Midi). The piste total is modest (~150km) but the off-piste is the best in the Alps. The Compagnie des Guides de Chamonix (founded 1821) is the most prestigious guiding company in the Alps. The Vallee Blanche (20km, 2,800m vertical) is the most famous ski run in the world.

stats.glacier: Mer de Glace glacier accessible via Montenvers railway

weather_snow.note: Valley floor altitude (1,035m) means lower runs can be slushy. High glacier terrain holds snow into summer. Best snow Jan-Mar.
weather_snow.glacier: Mer de Glace — accessible via Montenvers cog railway

villages.name: Chamonix Centre
villages.character: Real town with banks, supermarkets, shops, 100+ restaurants, bars, clubs, casino. Aiguille du Midi cable car starts from town centre. Historic quarter, 19th-century architecture.

villages.name: Les Praz
villages.character: Quiet hamlet at foot of Flegere, more peaceful, closer to Grands Montets

villages.name: Le Lavancher
villages.character: Small hamlet, limited amenities, very quiet

separate_ski_areas.Brevent-Flegere: Linked via cable car. Brevent has excellent intermediate cruising and the iconic Chamonix views of Mont Blanc. Flegere hides incredible off-piste couloirs with a guide.
separate_ski_areas.Grands Montets (Argentiere): Best advanced/expert terrain — steep couloirs, off-piste bowls, the famous 'Bochon' 'Chard' 'Yorkshire' and the 'Pas de Chevre' glacier run. Bluebird powder day here = best day of skiing of your life.
separate_ski_areas.Le Tour / Balme: Higher and more snow-sure. Good for intermediates, family-friendly. L'Alpage mountain farmhouse restaurant (old farmhouse, excellent cuisine).
separate_ski_areas.Les Houches: South-facing, sunny, lower altitude, family-friendly. Linked to Saint-Gervais. Good for beginners and sunny spring days.
separate_ski_areas.Vallee Blanche: 20km off-piste glacier descent from Aiguille du Midi (3,842m). The most famous ski run in the world. Guide essential. Requires fitness and good technique. Down to the valley floor at Chamonix.
separate_ski_areas.Courmayeur (Italy): Ski to Italy via the Vallee Blanche or heliski. Courmayeur is accessible from Chamonix for a day trip.

non_ski_activities.aiguille_du_midi: Highest cable car in France (3,842m). Step into the Void — glass box suspended over 1,000m drop. Panoramic views of Mont Blanc, the Alps, Italy. Book early to avoid queues.
non_ski_activities.mer_de_glace: Montenvers cog railway — train to the Mer de Glace glacier. Ice cave inside the glacier (carved annually).
spas: Heliopic Hotel & Spa (Mont Blanc views, sauna, steam room, cold plunge, hot tub, pool, massages)
QC Terme Spa (Italian-style thermal spa, outdoor pools with mountain views, hammam, relaxation areas)
non_ski_activities.swimming: Indoor pool at Centre Sportif Richard Bozon
non_ski_activities.ice_skating: Indoor ice rink at Centre Sportif
non_ski_activities.climbing: Indoor climbing wall + outdoor mountaineering routes
non_ski_activities.paragliding: Tandem flights from Brevent and other launch points — stunning Mont Blanc views
non_ski_activities.heliski: Heliski to/from Italy — Gran Paradiso and Vallee Blanche
non_ski_activities.ski_touring: Haute Route from Chamonix to Zermatt (5-7 day classic traverse)
non_ski_activities.shopping: Full year-round town shopping — outdoor gear to luxury brands, patisseries, fromageries
non_ski_activities.museums: Musee Alpin (mountain history), Mont Blanc exhibition
non_ski_activities.events: World Mountain Bike Championships, Marathon du Mont Blanc

signature: Atmosphere (veranda over river, exceptional carpaccio, espresso martinis)
Le Cap Horn (French-Japanese fusion, hushed alpine cabin)
Le Matafan (Hotel Mont Blanc, elevated, exceptional service)
Rose du Pont (oysters, caviar, Mont Blanc views, terrace)
dining_guide.traditional: La Caleche (40 years, fondue/raclette/tartiflette, warm characterful dining room)
dining_guide.microbrewery: Micro Brasserie de Chamonix (craft beer brewed on-site, lively informal setting, best apres stop)

apres_guide.vibe: Most varied nightlife of any French ski town. Rowdy bars, quiet wine bars, microbrewery, casino. Social and unpretentious — suits the mountaineering crowd. Not a champagne terrace scene.
apres_guide.bars: Micro Brasserie, Le Vermont (live music), diverse options across town

honest_drawbacks: Piste skiing is patchy — only ~150km across 5 disconnected sectors
Not ski-in/ski-out — each sector is a bus or drive away
Crowded lift queues at Brevent and Aiguille du Midi
Slower gondolas compared to modern systems
Valley floor altitude (1,035m) means lower snow can be thin
Can feel overwhelming — complex transport between areas
ski_school: Compagnie des Guides de Chamonix (founded 1821, most prestigious in Alps). Also Evolution 2 and Ski Sensations for on-piste instruction.
cross_border: Ski to Italy via Vallee Blanche or heliski to Courmayeur. Easy day trip to Courmayeur for Italian food and different terrain.
spas_specific: Nuxe Spa — Heliopic Hotel & Spa (Mont Blanc views, indoor-outdoor pool, sauna, steam room, cold plunge, hot tub, massages)
QC Terme Spa & Resorts (Italian-style thermal spa, outdoor pools, mountain views, hammam)
Cinq Monde Spa — Hôtel le Prieuré
bars_specific: MBC Pub (Canadian, craft beer brewed in-house with glacier water)
La Folie Douce Chamonix (vibrant terrace, panoramic Mont Blanc views)
Brev'Bar (Brévent slopes, front-row Mont Blanc views)
Le Shack Restaurant & Bar (Asian-fusion snacking, cocktails)
Bistrot des Sports (traditional bistro + sports bar)
